meta.title: Stop Buying $7 Coffee — Make These 5 Vietnamese Coffee Drinks at Home
meta.description:
You don’t need a $1000 espresso machine to make incredible coffee at home.

In this video, I’m showing you how to make 5 iconic Vietnamese coffee drinks using one simple tool — the phin filter.

From the bold, nostalgic cà phê sữa đá to the rich, dessert-like egg coffee, and the viral salt coffee (cà phê muối), these are the drinks that define Vietnamese coffee culture — and once you try them, your regular coffee might not hit the same anymore.

If you grew up seeing that orange Café du Monde tin on the counter, or you’ve ever sat on a tiny stool in Saigon watching coffee slowly drip into a glass… you already know — this isn’t just coffee. It’s a ritual.

And if you didn’t grow up with it, you’re about to.

☕ In this video:
00:56 Cà phê đen (Vietnamese black coffee)
03:11 Cà phê sữa đá (iced coffee with condensed milk)
03:42 Cà phê trứng (egg coffee)
05:05 Bạc xỉu (Vietnamese milk coffee)
06:11 Cà phê muối (salt coffee)
07:17 Cà phê cốt dừa (Vietnamese Coconut Coffee)

Correction:
06:27 Should be 1/8 tsp of fine sea salt!

If you’re into authentic Vietnamese food, coffee, and culture — subscribe.
We’re just getting started.

1. 4 Shots of Espresso( ristretto) : You need the extra caffeine to stand up to the sweetness.
2. 6 Pumps of White Mocha: This is our “Sữa” (condensed milk) substitute.
3. Fill Half & Half to the 2nd Line: This adds the creamy body that mimics the “Double-Bloom” richness.
4. Add Ice: Make sure they leave enough room so it doesn’t get watered down!
